title: Minimum Window Substring → wrap-around variant
label: multi
statement: Given strings `s` and `t`, return the **smallest substring of `s` that contains every character of `t`**, counting repeats (`t = "aa"` needs two `a`s). Return `""` if there is none; if several are equally short, the leftmost.
provenance: Reported in a LinkedIn **Staff** loop (Jun 2025, LeetCode Discuss) "with an extended condition where the source string is wrapped around", in an onsite in Sep 2026 (FastPrep), and in other LeetCode Discuss reports alongside Max Consecutive Ones III. Stage 2 is the wrap-around variant in my words.

clarify: For the follow-up: may the window wrap from the end of s back to the start? (Stage 2.)

stages.title: Minimum window
stages.say: Find the smallest window of s that contains every character of t.
stages.require: Implement `MinWindow.Find(s, t)`. Null or empty input → "".

stages.title: The string wraps around
stages.say: Now s is circular: a window may run past the end and continue from the start.
stages.require: Add `MinWindow.FindCircular(s, t)` returning the window text (it may wrap).
testNames: wraps: A at the end, BC at the start
a window longer than s is not allowed

prompts.label: Check my design — no code
prompts.text: I believe a sliding window with a count of characters still missing grows right until nothing is missing, then shrinks left while that stays true — O(|s| + |t|); the wrap-around version runs the same window over s+s and rejects windows longer than s. learn.title: 1 · Problem
learn.md: Given strings `s` and `t`, return the **smallest substring of `s` that contains every character of `t`**, counting repeats (`t = "aa"` needs two `a`s). Return `""` if there is none; if several are equally short, the leftmost.

learn.title: 2 · Clarifications
learn.md:
- Do repeats in t count? (Yes.)
- Case-sensitive? (Yes.)
- Leftmost on ties? (Yes.)
- For the follow-up: may the window wrap from the end of s back to the start? (Stage 2.)

learn.title: 3 · Key insight
learn.md: Keep one number — how many characters of t are still missing. Growing the right edge can only lower it; shrinking the left edge can only raise it. So every window is visited by two pointers that each move n times.

learn.title: 4 · Approach
learn.md: I would say, before coding: "A." sliding window with a count of characters still missing grows right until nothing is missing, then shrinks left while that stays true — O(|s| + |t|); the wrap-around version runs the same window over s+s and rejects windows longer than s."

learn.title: 12 · Common AI mistakes
learn.md:
- Checking the whole count map on every step (O(|charset|) per move).
- Ignoring repeated characters in t.
- For wrap-around: concatenating s+s and forgetting that a window longer than s is not valid.
- Returning the first window found instead of the smallest.
